title: Platform economics scripts & competitive anchors for inference
content:
Purpose: lightweight scripting and competitive anchors for field sellers who need to quickly translate Redwood's inference economics advantages into concise rebuttals, demo hooks, and POC asks. Aim: 90-second framing + 3 quick proof points + 2 demo flows + escalation questions for technical buyers.

Audience: AE/SE pair pre-demo, Solutions Engineers prepping for discovery call, Strategic sellers in SMB->Enterprise motion.

Topline 90s opener (anchored on economics + reliability):
- "Most vendors sell models; we sell predictable inference economics. Redwood lets you pick the trade-offs you want — lowest latency, lowest cost, or strict isolation — and measure the impact in tokens-per-dollar across real traffic patterns."
- Quick follow: "That means fewer surprise bills, fewer cold-starts during spikes, and a migration path from sandbox to dedicated capacity without rewriting your integration."

Three short proof points to use in any conversation:
1) Transparent unit economics: token-level breakdowns per-route and per-model in Console; show sample usage graph and per-token cost estimate.
2) Predictable capacity: Dedicated pools with SLA-backed latency windows vs shared endpoints (noisy-neighbor risk).
3) Quality-preserving optimizations: batching + prefix caching + mixed-precision quantization recommendations that reduce cost 2x–4x for typical chat workloads without re-training.

Common competitor claims + short counters (one-liners for AEs):
- "We have simpler pricing." -> "Simple can hide variance. We surface the unit drivers (tokens, sequence length, cache hit rate) so you can optimize rather than guess. Customers appreciate a bill they can model in spreadsheets."
- "We have the newest/open models available first." -> "We mirror the open ecosystem but add serving profiles and verified latency/cost benchmarks so you can deploy safely — newest models are great, but production is about predictable performance."
- "Managed endpoints are easier; just give us a model and call it a day." -> "Ease of onboarding is important — we keep the integration simple while adding controls (routing, rollouts, graceful fallback) that prevent outages when traffic patterns change."

Feature contrast highlights to bring to an SE call (prep bullets):
- Observability: per-route token breakdown, latency P50/P95, KV cache hit rate vs competitors' coarse metrics.
- Rollouts: canary/A-B + automatic fallback policies vs manual model swaps.
- Pricing flexibility: hosted pay-as-you-go vs reserved Dedicated capacity with burst windows and commit discounts.
- Private deployments: VPC/on-prem options + KMS integrations for regulated customers — competitor X rarely has true on-prem packaged support.

Demo hooks (2 short flows):
1) Cost-to-quality demo (~10 mins)
   - Setup: two routes, same prompt distribution. Route A -> standard hosted model. Route B -> Dedicated pool + caching enabled + 8-bit quantized variant.
   - Show: live token-per-response metric, console cost prediction, and latency P95 before/after enabling cache.
   - Ask: "If we could cut your per-response cost by 35% while preserving P95 under your 300ms threshold, would you consider a 30-day pilot?"

2) Reliability play demo (~8 mins)
   - Setup: simulate spike traffic (replay) and show smart routing policy fallback to lower-cost model variant with negligible quality drop.
   - Show: automatic fallback behavior in Console + alerting and rollback timeline.
   - Ask: "How often have you had to scramble because a single noisy job degraded latency for your customers?"

Objection map (detailed):
- Objection: "We're worried about vendor lock-in."
  - Quick rebuttal: "We support standard APIs and let you pin models/versions; our routing and rollout controls are implemented at the infra layer — you can migrate models with the same API hooks. We also provide exportable routing configs and a documented migration plan."
  - Technical ask: "Would your infra team want to see a sample routing config and migration runbook?"

- Objection: "Hosted costs could spike unpredictably."
  - Quick rebuttal: "Use Dedicated pools for predictable unit economics or set hard quotas/budgets per route — Console will show projected spend if usage continues. We also offer billing alerts and pre-paid reserved commitments to cap exposure."
  - Technical ask: "What's an acceptable monthly variance for your finance team? We'll propose a reserved vs burst plan to fit that band."

- Objection: "Open-source model parity and freshness matter more than infra."
  - Quick rebuttal: "We don't compete with models; we enable them. Our value is removing the ops burden so you can evaluate new models faster with less risk (benchmarks, verified latency, quantization profiles)."
  - Technical ask: "Which models are you actively evaluating? we'll run a quick perf/cost benchmark for those exact versions."

Traps / red flags sellers should call out (warning language + suggested probing):
- No per-route observability: If vendor can't show tokens-per-route or cache hit rates, call out the risk of hidden costs.
- Hand-wavy autoscaling: Ask for concrete SLA numbers and past incident postmortems; vague autoscaling = likely cold-start behavior.
- Single-region footprint for regulated customers: probe data residency and VPC/on-prem options early.
- Lack of rollbacks/feature flags: vendors that only support manual swaps increase blast radius for deployments.

POC asks (technical acceptance criteria to propose with customer):
- Baseline: 7 days of traffic capture + replay for representative route(s).
- Success metrics: <10% latency regression vs baseline, >=20% cost reduction per token or per-conversation depending on contract, no more than one incident requiring manual intervention during the pilot.
- Deliverables: console access, per-route cost dashboard, routing policy docs, sample rollback plan.

Quick scripts (copy-paste friendly)
- Finance-safe opener: "We can run a 14-day pilot using your real traffic in a sandboxed Dedicated pool with projected spend capped. We'll deliver a token-by-token cost breakdown and a recommendation to hit your target TCO."
- Security-heavy buyer: "We have a VPC/private option and KMS/HSM integrations; if you need air-gapped packaging we can scope that as an enterprise pilot."

Open questions for product/SE/infra (left for follow-up):
- Can Console export an automated migration plan (routing + model pins) as a JSON? (SEs asked for an 'export' feature)
- Need an example of reserved commit sizing guidance template for mid-market customers (30–200 CCUs).
- Is there a canonical KB article we can reference that quantifies cost delta from caching + quantization for chat vs embeddings workloads?

Next steps / playbook items (owner tags):
- SEs: bundle a 10-min cost-to-quality demo recording and attach to the outreach template. (owner: Ethan)
- GTM Ops: create a one-pager for finance that maps usage bands -> recommended reserved vs hosted approach. (owner: Sofia)
- Product: decide feasibility of Console 'export routing/migration' by Q2. (owner: Liam)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this short during calls — sellers hate long monologues. Use demo to prove, not preach.
- Have benchmark snapshots for 3 common archetypes: chat app, semantic search, summarization pipeline.
- Use customer language: "unit economics", "predictable spend", "SLA-backed latency" rather than deep infra jargon unless SE is in the room.
